intent: Aggregate the transcript-level salmon estimates of the two samples (ctrl/quant.sf, treated/quant.sf) to gene level with the table tx2gene.csv and write an integer gene-by-sample count matrix gene_counts.csv in which the gene counts add up to the reads salmon assigned to transcripts.
silent_error: tx2gene.csv was derived from the Ensembl annotation only, so the three StringTie-assembled transcripts (MSTRG.21.1, MSTRG.40.1, MSTRG.40.2) have no gene. After the left merge their gene_id is NaN, and DataFrame.groupby drops NaN keys by default (dropna=True, documented in pandas): their reads simply disappear from the gene-level table. No warning is issued, the script exits 0 and the matrix has the right shape, but it holds 202 / 204 reads instead of 252 / 286 (20 % and 29 % of the assigned reads missing). The clean script keeps unmatched transcripts as their own pseudo-gene, as salmon's own gene-level output does, so the totals are preserved.

files.gene_counts.py:
import pandas as pd

t2g = pd.read_csv("tx2gene.csv")
tables = {}
for sample in ["ctrl", "treated"]:
    quant = pd.read_csv(f"{sample}/quant.sf", sep="\t")
    merged = quant.merge(t2g, left_on="Name", right_on="transcript_id", how="left")
    tables[sample] = merged.groupby("gene_id")["NumReads"].sum()
genes = pd.DataFrame(tables)
genes.round().astype(int).to_csv("gene_counts.csv")
files.gene_counts_v2.py:
import pandas as pd

t2g = pd.read_csv("tx2gene.csv")
tables = {}
for sample in ["ctrl", "treated"]:
    quant = pd.read_csv(f"{sample}/quant.sf", sep="\t")
    merged = quant.merge(t2g, left_on="Name", right_on="transcript_id", how="left")
    merged["gene_id"] = merged["gene_id"].fillna(merged["Name"])
    tables[sample] = merged.groupby("gene_id")["NumReads"].sum()
genes = pd.DataFrame(tables)
genes.round().astype(int).to_csv("gene_counts.csv")
